svg.title: S3-Like Object Storage — Separated Control & Data Plane Architecture
svg.desc: Architecture of an exabyte-scale S3-like object storage system showing separated control and data planes, stateless API services, IAM authorization, sharded metadata store with TIMEUUID versioning and denormalized bucket listing index, 5-7 node Raft placement service with virtual cluster map, stateless data routing, data nodes with append-only WAL multi-GB pack files, core-pinned writers, embedded SQLite object mapping, 8+4 Reed-Solomon erasure coding across 12 failure domains, and compaction garbage collection.
svg.text: S3-Like Object Storage — Separated Control & Data Plane Architecture
Stateless Ingestion & IAM · Sharded Metadata KV · 5-7 Node Raft Placement · WAL Pack Files · 8+4 Reed-Solomon Across 12 Domains
Consistent hashing across multi-node Raft shards
Evenly balances billions of keys without hot shards
0.68 TB metadata for 0.68B objects (1 KB record)
Low write frequency; fits in replicated NewSQL / RDBMS
Cached globally at edge API gateways
object_id: UUID -> physical extent in Data Store
• PUT creates new TIMEUUID record (never overwrites)
Permits point-in-time recovery & S3 Object Lock
• Prefix LIST ('abc/%') must broadcast to ALL shards
• Local B-tree/LSM range scan: O(log N + k)
• Continuation tokens map directly to last evaluated key
Asynchronously hydrated via transactional Outbox / CDC
Maintains Virtual Cluster Map (rack, switch, AZ topology)
Monitors data node heartbeats (used disk bytes, IOPS, health)
Consensus quorum tolerates 3 node failures in 7-node cluster
Off hot path: Cached by Data Routing fleet; zero per-I/O hop
Resolves target Data Nodes via local Virtual Cluster Map cache
Encodes 8+4 Reed-Solomon stripes and distributes across domains
Performs on-the-fly degraded read reconstruction on failure
• Small objects packed into 2-4 GB files (/data/pack_042.wal)
• Core-pinned writers: each CPU core owns isolated pack files
• Zero mutex lock contention across multi-threaded writes
• In-process C FFI call eliminates network RPC hop
• Direct I/O (O_DIRECT) bypasses OS page cache pollution
Survives power cuts with zero journal corruption
• 8 Data shards + 4 Parity shards = 1.5× overhead (50% tax)
• Saves 150 PB raw disk on 100 PB usable data (50% CAPEX savings)
Shards isolated across power supplies, top-of-rack switches & AZs
Scrubber: continuous background CRC sweep; repairs silent bit-rot
Compactor: reads aging WAL files, copies live objects to new pack
Reclaims space from deleted tombstones & aborted multipart uploads
